gate: W5_PLACEMENT_V1 - dedicated-main W5 counterexample pilot: is the W6 straggler caused by the main and the sixth worker sharing CPU 0?
classification: FCC_N SCENARIO FAMILY - NOT THE 2/3-ATOM CERTIFICATION SCOPE

baseline.this_branch: claude/w5-placement-pilot-v1 in the main checkout (no worktree)

machine_topology_checked_before_seal.result: 6 physical cores, 6 logical CPUs, no SMT, one processor group; core k owns exactly logical CPU k (k = 0..5)
machine_topology_checked_before_seal.meaning: 'shared CPU 0' in W6 = the main process and worker 6 time-share one physical core (not SMT siblings)
machine_topology_checked_before_seal.rechecked: the campaign records the same topology at its start and refuses to run if it differs

hypothesis: In E2_PAIR_PARALLEL_V1 W6 the worker pinned to CPU 0 (shared with the main) was the slowest worker (e.g. N=24 E1: 6.55 s vs 5.5-5.9 s). If the sharing is the bottleneck, W5 with a dedicated main core should be as fast as W6 or faster, with less CPU.
unchanged_contract: evaluator E2 = rw:R1+R2 only; physics, all pairs, no cutoff, KDK, dt, mass, domain, rounding/readout, p = 128, FCC_N initial-state rule, the E2_PAIR_PARALLEL_V1 parallel algorithm (experiments/e2_pair_parallel_v1/run.run_parallel imported unchanged) and the MULTIATOM serial path (experiments/multiatom_parallel_v1/run.run_serial imported unchanged). Only CPU placement and worker count differ.
execution_plan: every run is described by an ExecutionPlan {evaluator, precision, backend, worker_count, main_cpu, worker_cpus}; backend CPU_SERIAL and CPU_PARALLEL are implemented by delegating to the unchanged runners; GPU is a reserved backend name that raises NotImplementedError (no GPU code in this step)

W4_DEDICATED.role: near control (main also alone on its core)

W6_SHARED.role: existing layout: worker 6 shares core 0 with the main

configurations.campaign_process: pinned to CPU 0; it only launches runs and waits (disclosed: it is on the main's core in every configuration)

scope.order: per repetition: N ascending; within each N the 4 configurations [SER_E2, W4_DEDICATED, W5_DEDICATED, W6_SHARED] rotated by the repetition index
scope.no_additions: no N, T, p or configuration is added after seeing results; further experiments need a separate protocol
scope.estimated_cost: about 1,600 CPU s and 22 min wall on the laptop; cap 5,000 CPU s

load_contamination_rule: same as E2_PAIR_PARALLEL_V1: 1 s snapshot before every (N, repetition) group excluding the own process tree and the System Idle Process; CONTAMINATED if other processes sum >= 100 % of one logical CPU or a python/roblox/codex/node process >= 25 %. Contaminated groups are kept, checked for correctness and excluded from performance numbers.
measurements_per_run: end-to-end wall, loop wall, ready/spawn wall, total CPU (QueryProcessCycleTime / calibrated rate) and its main / per-worker split, tick CPU, per-worker busy wall, main send / wait / reduce / KDK+other, peak working set per process, main and worker affinity (requested, child read-back, parent pin, at exit), outcome / completed steps / stop kind / stop step / cells / endpoints key / initial-state digest
correctness: for each N: W4, W5, W6 (all repetitions) bit-identical to SER_E2 (and SER_E2 identical across repetitions) in completed steps, stop kind, stop step, cells, the full endpoints key and the initial-state digest; SER_E2 also equal to the E2_PAIR_PARALLEL_V1 SER_E2 record of the same N. Any mismatch -> verdict D, performance judgement stops.

verdict_rules (per N, on clean repetitio.B: W6 end-to-end wall is faster than W5 by >= 3 % (median) and W6 is faster in >= 4 of 5 paired repetitions
verdict_rules (per N, on clean repetitio.A: not B, W5 end-to-end wall <= W6 x 1.02 (median), and W5 total CPU is lower than W6 by >= 3 % (median) and lower in >= 4 of 5 paired repetitions
verdict_rules (per N, on clean repetitio.overall: reported per N; no single overall winner is declared unless all three N agree

analysis_questions.Q1: W5 vs W6 end-to-end and loop wall (median, paired sign count)
analysis_questions.Q3: W4 -> W5 -> W6 loop speedup vs SER_E2 and efficiency; 'normal' = wall decreases with W and efficiency decreases slowly; an increase of wall with W, or an efficiency jump, is flagged
analysis_questions.Q4: in W6, in how many repetitions is the CPU-0 worker (index 5) the maximum busy-wall worker, and its excess over the median of the other five
analysis_questions.Q5: per configuration: worker busy-wall spread (max - min) / median
analysis_questions.Q6: main send / wait / reduce / KDK+other per configuration
analysis_questions.Q7: per N: is W6 loop wall >= W5 loop wall (sixth worker adds more contention than compute)?

claims_forbidden: a laptop result holds for the desktop (SMT) or other machines
